<explanation>
1. Project type and purpose  
   - This is a full-stack documentation website (docs.github.com) built with Next.js (React + Node/TypeScript).  
   - It ingests Markdown content (in content/, data/ and assets/), transforms it via content-render, content-linter, and other pipelines, then serves it through a Next.js server with dynamic API routes (article-api, REST, GraphQL, search, audit-logs, secret-scanning, webhooks, etc.).  
   - CI/CD is orchestrated by GitHub Actions, and production runs in Docker/Kubernetes behind a CDN (Fastly).

2. Main components  
   a. Source content & data  
     - content/, data/, assets/: Markdown, YAML, CSV source files  
     - data-directory, automated-pipelines, ghes-releases, etc.: scripts to validate/generate derived JSON/HTML  
   b. Build & CI/CD  
     - .github/workflows: lint, test, build, deploy pipelines  
     - Dockerfile + docker-compose + .devcontainer: containerize for local dev and staging/prod  
   c. Core application  
     - Next.js frontend (src/frame + src/pages): React pages and dynamic route handlers  
     - API routes (under src/*-api, src/rest, src/graphql, src/search, etc.): serverless/Express-style functions  
     - Shared libraries (src/content-render, src/content-linter, src/assets, src/data-directory)  
   d. Infrastructure & deployment  
     - config/kubernetes: manifests for webapp Deployment + Service  
     - config/moda: feature-flag & environment configs  
     - External services: Elasticsearch cluster for site search; Fastly for CDN & remote JSON caching; optional S3/minio for assets  
   e. Tests & monitoring  
     - src/tests, fixtures, vitest.config.ts: unit, integration, e2e (Playwright)  
     - observability: StatsD, error handling, failbot  
     - workflows: slack alerts, dead link checks

3. Component interactions  
   - Developer → GitHub → GitHub Actions (CI): runs content-linter, tests, builds artifacts → pushes Docker image  
   - Kubernetes (Production & Staging): pulls image → runs Next.js server + API routes  
   - CDN (Fastly) sits in front of the Next.js origin, caching both pages and remote JSON endpoints  
   - Next.js server’s API routes query:  
     • local JSON (generated under public or via remotejson) for content, data, assets  
     • Elasticsearch for general and AI search  
     • static JSON schemas for REST/GraphQL docs  
   - Client browsers fetch pages + assets via CDN; JS hydration for interactive features

4. Architectural patterns & principles  
   - Monorepo with clear separation of concerns: content, data pipelines, services, frontend  
   - “Headless CMS” approach: Markdown + JSON → API → page rendering  
   - Next.js Server-Side Rendering + Dynamic Routes for versioned docs  
   - Feature-flag driven code (config/moda, useFeatureFlags hook)  
   - Microservices-within-Next.js: each subfolder under src/*-api or src/* acts as its own API endpoint  
   - Kubernetes + GitOps for deployments

5. Tailoring the diagram for this full-stack app  
   - Draw three tiers:  
     • Content & Data Layer (Markdown, YAML, CSV, JSON source files + pipeline scripts)  
     • Application Layer (Next.js server & API Routes, Dynamic Rendering, React UI Components)  
     • Infrastructure Layer (CI/CD, Docker/Kubernetes, CDN, External Services)  
   - Show content pipelines as a linear flow: content/ → content-render + content-linter + data-directory → generated JSON → served by Next.js  
   - Highlight the API boundary between front-end (client) and back-end (API routes).  
   - Include search: client → Next.js search API → Elasticsearch.  
   - Include CDN caching of pages and remote JSON.

6. Diagram elements to include  
   - Components (boxes) labeled:  
     • Content Store (Markdown, data, assets)  
     • Build Pipeline (GitHub Actions)  
     • Next.js Server (Frontend + API Routes)  
     • CDN / Edge Cache (Fastly)  
     • Kubernetes Cluster (Pods + Services)  
     • Search Cluster (Elasticsearch)  
     • Storage (S3 / Minio for assets)  
   - Arrows for data flow:  
     • commits → CI → Docker image  
     • image → Kubernetes → Next.js  
     • client requests → CDN → Next.js → APIs → Data/ES  
   - Colors/shapes:  
     • Blue for source/content  
     • Green for compute (server, API)  
     • Orange for external services (ES, CDN)  
     • Gray for infrastructure (CI/CD, Kubernetes)  
   - Directional arrows for request/response and build/deploy flows.

7. Detail & completeness  
   - Capture versioning: Next.js dynamic routes /[version]/[product]/…  
   - Show major API modules as sub-components under the application box  
   - Annotate any feature-flags or experimental middleware layers (early-access, experiments)  
   - Don’t overcomplicate: group related API routes into logical services (Article API, REST API, GraphQL API, Search API, Asset API, Audit Logs, etc.)  
   - Emphasize the static vs dynamic boundaries: static content can be pre-built; others served on-demand.

Use this outline to draft a layered architecture diagram that maps the project’s repo structure to runtime components, their interactions, and the supporting infrastructure. Ensure each box is clearly labeled, arrows show flow, and color coding distinguishes layer types.
